ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Dwight D. Eisenhower — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: One-year review after myocardial infarction: end of dual antiplatelet therapy

text.paragraph: Mr. Eisenhower returns one year after his myocardial infarction. He has had no chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, or bleeding, and has not needed nitroglycerin. He works full time, travels, and plays golf twice a week. He did not get the basic metabolic panel ordered for July because he was travelling. He asks whether he can now stop ticagrelor, which bruises him, and whether he still needs metoprolol. [S]

list.item:
Myocardial infarction one year ago (I25.2). Twelve months of dual antiplatelet therapy completed without major bleeding. [S]
Stop ticagrelor today; continue aspirin 81 mg daily for life.
Continue metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily: his ejection fraction recovered to 52 percent, so the beta-blocker is now continued for his hypertension and blood pressure control, which are good on it.

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). LDL cholesterol 49 mg/dL, at goal. [S]
Continue atorvastatin and ezetimibe; lipid panel yearly.

Essential hypertension (I10). Blood pressure 124/74 mmHg. Potassium 4.5 and eGFR 82 on lisinopril. [S]
No change; basic metabolic panel every six months, with a reminder.

Former heavy cigarette smoker (Z87.891). Abstinent about seven years. [S]
Discuss lung cancer and abdominal aortic aneurysm screening at next month's annual wellness visit.
